title: Drug billers paid far more per claim than California peers
question: Which San Francisco billers were paid far more per Medicaid drug claim line, or per beneficiary-month, than California billers of the same registered type?
finding: 252 San Francisco billing numbers drew $207.4 million of Medicaid drug money in the national file from 2018 to 2024 ($19.9 million in 2018, $48.9 million in 2024), against $8.06 billion for California. 3 stand above 99 in 100 California peers per claim line or per beneficiary-month in a year with $250,000 or more (2 outside City government and the University of California); the largest is SCRIPTSITE PHARMACY PARTNERS LLC ($527,644 in 2019, $1,609 per line against $49 for the middle peer).
how: The national file (21,515,000 rows, one per billing number, prescribing number, drug code and month, 2018 to 2024) was read straight from the zip. 1,135,323 rows whose drug code is one digit repeated, a placeholder for a missing code, were dropped as the federal documentation advises: they carry a sum of $20,382.56 billion, which is not real money. A provider number counts as San Francisco when the California part of the national provider registry puts its practice address in San Francisco (252 billing numbers with drug money); California peers are all billing numbers in that registry file. A drug product is the first nine digits of the code (maker and product), package sizes added together; names come from Open Payments and Part D files that print a name beside a code. Peers: California billing numbers with $50,000 or more of drug money that year and the same primary registry type (taxonomy code) where at least 20 such peers exist, otherwise the same kind (pharmacy, by registry type codes beginning 3336 as the medicare download notes record, or other). Each biller is shown on its largest flagged year.
limits: Nothing here names or counts a patient; the file withholds small cells. The file mixes pharmacy claims with drugs given in clinics and amounts health plans report, does not drop denied claims, and counts claim lines, not quantities: a line for a 90-day supply or a high dose costs more without anything being wrong. Beneficiary-months add up each month’s count of people, so a person treated every month counts twelve times. A specialty pharmacy serving people with HIV, hepatitis or cancer, a hospital clinic, a fertility or eye practice will rightly stand far above an ordinary pharmacy. 2024 is preliminary. The registry places a provider by its address today.
